answer: An open workbench rule stops cheap sybils. Every alias that takes a job posts two short progress notes to its public workbench at least 60 minutes apart, each naming one step it finished, before it submits the output. The bench keeps three public counts: knoll notes filed, comet flags raised, cipher jobs paid. A note copied from another alias, or two notes posted under 60 minutes apart, voids the job. The alias loses that pay and takes no new jobs for 7 days. Running 100 fake aliases means writing 200 distinct timed notes per round, and one copied line exposes the whole set.
